thread:
incident-bot: PAGING oncall: prod/runtime latency alert -> p95 token latency > 2.1s (traffic spike) across us-east-1. Auto-escalation: potential batching/kernel fallback after recent rollout. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/prod/runtime/overview :rotating_light:

sanjay.k: acked — oncall here, looking. tagged eng-runtime and eng-sre. gathering quick context.

oncall-bot: oncall handover: sanjay.k is primary for the next 2h. See runbook: /runbooks/runtime-latency.md

mike_r: saw the alert — rolling release wave (wave-2026-03-17-08) introduced batcher_v2 + kernel-selector changes at 08:05. Canary passed but post-rollout saw p95 jump.

jess: logs on a few hosts show kernel fallback to "compat-quant" and frequent eviction events in the batcher. snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T08:18:12Z] node-123 kernel_selector: fallback -> compat-quant (latency 5.4ms)
[2026-03-17T08:18:12Z] node-123 batcher: evict batch_id=7 size=64 -> 0 (timeout)
```

carla_ops: customer-facing note: support queue seeing increased latency reports, roughly 2-4% elevated error/timeout. prepping PSAT.

sanjay.k: quick mitigation options: 1) flip feature flag batcher_v2 off (kill switch) 2) rollback wave-2026-03-17-08 3) temporarily route traffic to older capacity pool. Recommend trying FF kill first (fastest).

mike_r: +1 flip FF then monitor 5m. FF path: Admin Console -> Feature Flags -> batcher_v2 -> OFF or via CLI:
```
redwood-ctl ff set batcher_v2 false --env prod --wave wave-2026-03-17-08
```

jess: I'm on the FF console. prepping to flip in 30s. will annotate the change and keep it reversible.

carla_ops: note: if we flip FF, we should let support know to hold customer notifications until we have 10m of stable metrics.

jess: flipping now.

[system] jess toggled feature flag batcher_v2 -> OFF (comment: emergency kill-switch for post-rollout latency)

mike_r: observed immediate reduction in evictions on node-123, kernel-selector logs show fewer fallback events. Trending p95 down from 2.2s -> 1.0s within 90s.

sanjay.k: nice. keep monitoring 10m. if p95 doesn't stay <1.3s we escalate to rollback.

oncall-bot: Reminder: capture timestamps and correlated request IDs for customers impacted (support ticket tags).

carla_ops: quick calc from sampling: ~3.1% of requests during the 08:10-08:20 window exceeded SLA, mostly long-tail small-batch text-gen calls. I'll open a customer-impact summary after stabilization.

mike_r: also found a guardrail mismatch in the kernel-selector that allowed compat kernels for slice sizes > 128 when batcher_v2 is enabled; adding a temporary config patch but non-urgent now that FF is off. patch branch: fix/kernel-guard-2026-03

sanjay.k: action items: 1) Jess: keep FF off and watch for 15m 2) Mike: prepare rollback playbook steps if trend reverses 3) Carla: customer-impact note and postmortem stub. I'll update incident channel in 15.

carla_ops: draft for support (will post after 15m): "We observed elevated latency from 08:10-08:22 UTC due to a post-release batching/kernel interaction. We've applied an emergency feature-flag kill switch which reduced p95 and mitigated customer impact. We're monitoring and will follow up with details and timeline."

jess: after 15m p95 = 1.05s, errors back to baseline. No rollback required. Recommend leaving FF off until next safe patch wave.

sanjay.k: agreed. keeping FF off, flagged wave for rollback/patch. tagging eng-releases to block further rolls of batcher_v2 until kernel guard in.

mike_r: will push a small config guard and test in staging; plan to re-enable batcher_v2 behind stricter kernel selection in a canary-only rollout.

carla_ops: customer-impact summary posted to internal support: https://support.redwood/incident/1745556666 — notifying top 10 customers affected via outbound template.

sanjay.k: incident status -> mitigated, oncall will continue observation for 2h then hand off to eng-runtime for postmortem. Closing urgent paging. Great triage team. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident marked MITIGATED by sanjay.k at 1745557300. Postmortem task created: PM-1745556666.
